public_rationale: The condition has not been met. OpenAI described continuing operations on October 28, and reporting described Microsoft as a minority owner. These records do not disprove consequences predicted for a future failure. The conditional-forecast rule therefore requires not_adjudicable. limitations: Continuing operations do not establish long-term solvency.

No deadline permits failure to be inferred from elapsed time.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: When OpenAI dies it will likely fold into Microsoft, sharply cut compute demand, likely end free ChatGPT and raise prices.

statement.excerpt: When OpenAI dies — likely folding into Microsoft in the process — it will massively pull back on any and all compute demands, with the likely end of and free ChatGPT and a massive price bump across the board.

from_speaker: will massively pull back on any and all compute demands
the likely end of and free ChatGPT
a massive price bump across the board
our_interpretation: “Dies” means business failure resulting in shutdown, liquidation, or a distressed absorption that ends OpenAI's independent business. Ordinary restructuring or investment does not qualify.
The firm predictions are a large, broad reduction in compute demand and large price increases across the surviving paid offerings. Compute contraction alone cannot support the whole claim.
Absorption into Microsoft and ending free ChatGPT are separately qualified as likely. Their outcomes must be reported separately, without treating either as certain.
Read the apparent typo “end of and free ChatGPT” as ending free ChatGPT.

Compare compute demand and like-for-like prices immediately before failure with the implemented shutdown or successor operating arrangements. Include transferred workloads so a change in ownership cannot masquerade as reduced demand.
No percentage threshold or deadline is supplied. The nearby speculation about 2027 does not establish a deadline for this conditional claim.
criteria.support_condition: A qualifying failure occurs, followed by a clearly large reduction across OpenAI's compute demand and clearly large, broad increases in comparable paid-service prices. Assess whether Microsoft absorbs the business and whether free ChatGPT ends as additional, qualified predictions. Full support requires the observed package to match the claim; compute contraction alone is insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a qualifying failure, implemented successor arrangements preserve or increase compute demand, or preserve or reduce prices across continuing comparable paid offerings. Such evidence would contradict the corresponding firm prediction. Failure to join Microsoft or retention of free ChatGPT would count against the qualified predictions, with their weaker wording acknowledged.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI describes ongoing business operations on the evaluation date. This supports treating the failure antecedent as unmet; it does not test the predicted consequences of a future failure.
